result_text:
I changed the two mock-folder conventions in `ScopingConventions` so any folder starting with `mock` or `__mock` counts as test code. The new test and the related existing tests pass offline.

- **Change:** in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around line 393), the `__mock` and `mock` patterns now use `[^/]*` in place of `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`. That lets the rest of the folder name be anything, including no characters at all (plain `mock/`), punctuation and non-ASCII. The `/` delimiters still keep the match inside one folder, so `remock/`, `demo/` and `mock.java` or `mockery.java` files are not caught. Backslash paths already work because `SourceFileFilter` also tries a slash-normalised form of the path.
- **Kept:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` still match, and the separate `[Mm]ocks` convention is untouched.
- **Test:** new `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsMockTest.java`. It reads the registered "Mock resources" conventions by reflection and checks the positive and negative cases from the task, including the backslash path.

Test results: `ScopingConventionsMockTest` (2), `SourceFileFilterTest` (6) and `CodeConfigurationTest` (4) all pass. I did not run the full codeanalyzer suite.
